name: Greatfather Winter
summary: As winter turns, Greatfather Winter is part of old legend and city festivities. Some say he lays snow across Azeroth so the land may rest and renew. In the cities, goblins of Smokywood Pastures shape how people know him.

sections.title: Myth and Renewal
sections.body:
Ancient tales say Greatfather Winter wanders the world late in the year. He spreads his snowy cloak, and nature sleeps before it is born anew. Dwarves call him an aspect or herald of the titans. They point to Dun Morogh's frosted crags as proof of his favor. Tauren honor his place in winter's turning, while crediting the Sun and Moon with the cold and storms that let the Earth Mother rest.

Across the lands, people gather and feast against the cold. They hold to the promise that life will return.

sections.title: Smokywood Pastures and City Festivities
sections.body:
In Ironforge and Orgrimmar, goblins of Smokywood Pastures have reshaped the old spirit for city celebrations. The trading company made popular the image of Greatfather Winter as a cheerful elder in red, with a white beard, flying sleigh, holiday treats, and toys.

Smokywood Pastures hires a dwarf in Ironforge and an orc in Orgrimmar to hear children's wishlists and accept milk and gingerbread cookies. Beneath lavishly decorated trees, the company also promotes its seasonal wares.

faq.q: Is the Greatfather Winter in Ironforge the real spirit?
aliases: who is the guy in ironforge
faq.answer: The Greatfather Winter by Ironforge's festive tree is an actor hired by Smokywood Pastures. The goblin company stages these appearances to delight children and sell seasonal confections. Ancient legends tell of an ethereal being who walks the world in winter.

faq.q: Why do dwarves revere Greatfather Winter?
faq.answer: Dwarves connect Greatfather Winter with the titans, their creators. They see the snow he spreads as a blessing and point to Dun Morogh's perpetually frigid peaks as proof of his favor.

faq.q: What does Greatfather Winter do with the cookies and milk brought to him?
faq.answer: In Smokywood Pastures' holiday tales, Greatfather Winter snacks on gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk while reading wishlists and spreading holiday cheer.

faq.q: How does the Horde view Greatfather Winter?
faq.answer: In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures promotes the festivities with an orc portraying Greatfather Winter. Tauren respect winter as a time for the Earth Mother to rest and renew. They honor his part in the seasonal cycle without worshipping the titans.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you can see Greatfather Winter as an aspect of the titans who carved the world. Dun Morogh's snowy peaks bear witness to his touch.
As a cook, you can make gingerbread cookies and other festive treats for Smokywood Pastures and Greatfather Winter himself.
